builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AdaBool: Sparse Boolean Matrix Processing with Adaptive Data Representation
summary: AdaBool replaces monolithic sparse-matrix formats (e.g., CSR/CSC) with fine-grained per-block encodings chosen by local sparsity, plus a heterogeneous GPU execution model that groups blocks by encoding type. The cost is substantial engineering complexity: block partitioning, multiple encoding/decoding paths, custom low-level GPU kernels, and scheduling logic that must all be implemented and maintained, with no off-the-shelf library availability indicated. It can fail when matrices have near-uniform sparsity (negating the adaptive benefit), when block-granularity overhead exceeds compression gains on smaller matrices, or when the reader's workloads simply do not involve Boolean matrix multiplication.
rationale: The method targets sparse Boolean matrix kernels rather than LLM inference or training, so it is only relevant if the reader's production pipeline contains graph- or set-relation workloads expressible as SpBMM, and its custom-kernel implementation cost is hard to justify on constrained infrastructure without a confirmed matching bottleneck.
technique: Adaptive block-wise sparse Boolean matrix multiplication

claims.statement: AdaBool replaces monolithic sparse-matrix formats (e.g., CSR/CSC) with fine-grained per-block encodings chosen by local sparsity, plus a heterogeneous GPU execution model that groups blocks by encoding type. The cost is substantial engineering complexity: block partitioning, multiple encoding/decoding paths, custom low-level GPU kernels, and scheduling logic that must all be implemented and maintained, with no off-the-shelf library availability indicated. It can fail when matrices have near-uniform sparsity (negating the adaptive benefit), when block-granularity overhead exceeds compression gains on smaller matrices, or when the reader's workloads simply do not involve Boolean matrix multiplication.
Outperforms representative SpBMM baselines by over an order of magnitude on production and public workloads.
